title: Two Sum
prompt: Given a list of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return the indices `[i, j]` (with i < j) of the two numbers that add up to `target`. Exactly one solution exists.
hint: A dictionary mapping value to index lets you find the complement in one pass.

title: Valid Palindrome
prompt: Return True if string `s` reads the same forwards and backwards after keeping only letters and digits and ignoring case; otherwise False.

args: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama

space: O(n) or O(1) with two pointers
hint: Filter with str.isalnum() and compare to its reverse, or use two pointers.

title: FizzBuzz
prompt: Return a list of strings for numbers 1..n: 'Fizz' for multiples of 3, 'Buzz' for multiples of 5, 'FizzBuzz' for both, otherwise the number as a string.

title: Word Frequency
prompt: Return a dictionary mapping each lowercase word in `text` to its count. Words are separated by whitespace; strip the punctuation characters . , ! ? from word edges.
hint: Use dict.get or collections.Counter after normalising each word.

title: Maximum Subarray
prompt: Given a non-empty list of integers `nums`, return the largest sum of any contiguous subarray.
hint: Kadane's algorithm: best ending here = max(x, best_ending_here + x).

title: Valid Parentheses
prompt: Given a string `s` containing only ()[]{} characters, return True if every bracket is closed by the same type in the correct order.
hint: Use a stack and a mapping of closing to opening brackets.

title: Moving Average
prompt: Given a list of numbers `nums` and window size `k`, return a list of the average of each consecutive window of length k, each rounded to 2 decimals. Return [] if k is larger than the list.
hint: Maintain a running window sum instead of re-summing each window.

title: Merge Intervals
prompt: Given a list of [start, end] intervals, merge all overlapping intervals (touching intervals such as [1,2] and [2,3] overlap) and return the merged list sorted by start.
hint: Sort by start, then extend the last merged interval while the next one overlaps.
